newsitem.title: USA: Compuserve settles suit with Time magazine.
newsitem.headline: Compuserve settles suit with Time magazine.

text.p: CompuServe Corp has reached an "amicable resolution" with Time Magazine, Time Warner Inc's flagship publication, of a lawsuit concerning CompuServe's early termination of an original two-year contract, the companies announced Friday.
The two companies have also reached a financial compromise resulting from the agreement, but did not reveal specific terms, they said.
Under the agreement, Time Magazine content would be restored in CompuServe's CSi service, effective April 25, they said.
Further, Time's area on CSi will include an online version of the current edition of the magazine and features and stories from Time Daily and Time Digital, two other products of the publication.
Time will continue to manage the Time Forum areas in the CS1, they said.

"We are pleased that we have reached a mutually satisfactory agreement that allows us to further our valued relationship with Time," said Denny Matteucci, CompuServe's president of interactive services.
"Time is happy to continue its relationship with CompuServe and our readers on CompuServe," said Ken Godshall, Time's vice president of consumer marketing.
CompuServe provides online/Internet access through its CSi and SPRYNET brands. Time became the first online newsmagazine in 1993 and in 1994 was the first magazine launched on the Internet.
